chunks: Al-Ḥalabī narrated from him, from his father, peace be upon them both, who said:
If you have performed a salat while you are in the mosque, and the salat is then established, then if you wish, leave; and if you wish, perform salat with them and make it tasbih.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: the salat being established for congregation
key_terms.الْمَسْجِدِ: the mosque, the place where the person is present
key_terms.تَسْبِيحًا: an act of glorification and remembrance, not counted here as the obligatory salat
key_terms.فَأُقِيمَتِ: it was established, referring to the commencement of congregational salat
key_terms.فَاخْرُجْ: then leave, if one chooses not to join again
key_terms.فَصَلِّ: then perform salat, meaning join them in prayer

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if they have already prayed and then the congregational prayer is established in the mosque?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the ruling for one who has already performed salat in the mosque and then finds the congregational salat being established. It permits either leaving or joining the congregation again, with the repeated prayer counted as tasbih rather than an obligatory salat.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1214 - Al-Halabi narrated from the Imam (as) from his father (as) who said:

"If you have already prayed and you are in the mosque, and the congregational prayer is established, then if you wish, you may leave, or if you wish, you may pray with them and consider it as a form of tasbih (remembrance and glorification)."
